title: Symbol row reader is a prefix inverse
statement: Let $A$ be a type, and let a reader and writer for values in $A$ satisfy: for every $a\in A$ and bit string $x$, reading the encoding of $a$ followed by $x$ returns $(a,x)$. For every function $f$ assigning an element of $A$ to each of blank, $0$, and $1$, and every bit string $x$, the reader for a three-entry symbol row applied to the encodings of $f(\text{blank})$, $f(0)$, and $f(1)$ in that order, followed by $x$, returns $(f,x)$.
hypotheses_covered: Reading each written value followed by any suffix returns that value and suffix
A function from the three symbols blank, 0, and 1 to A
replaced:
Let a field reader and a field writer for values in a type $A$ be given such
that reading from any written value followed by any suffix returns exactly that
value and suffix.  Then for every function $f$ from the three tape symbols
(blank, $0$, $1$) to $A$ and every bit string $x$, the three-symbol row reader
applied to the concatenation of the written values $f(\mathrm{blank})$, $f(0)$,
$f(1)$ in that order, followed by $x$, succeeds and returns $(f, x)$.
